question: A UPS acceptance test includes:
choices: Static transfer from inverter to bypass and back
Tan delta of the battery jars only
Table 100.6 cable VLF in place of a function test
explanation: ATS 7.22.2 calls for the static transfer both ways, on normal load when you can. The pass criterion is the manufacturer’s data for that transfer, not a cable table.

question: Automatic transfer switch control wiring shall not be less than:
explanation: 7.22.3.D.3 is 2 MΩ on control wiring. Power-contact microhms are a different line. The generator’s polarization index does not grade the transfer-switch wiring.

question: An automatic transfer switch test is not finished when the relay picks up. ATS 7.22.3 also wants you to time:
choices: Delay on transfer, and delay plus retransfer when normal returns
explanation: The section lists time delay on transfer, the transfer itself, and time delay and retransfer when normal power returns. A contact closure in the test set does not prove the switch moved and came back.

question: During a UPS static-transfer test the inverter is the source and bypass is healthy. The test should show:
choices: Transfer to bypass and back, within the manufacturer’s time
That the bypass breaker is welded shut
Tan delta of the output cable instead of a transfer
explanation: ATS 7.22.2 wants the transfer both directions, preferably on real load, and the result compared with the UPS manual. A single transfer that never returns does not finish the test.

question: A step-up transformer can be back-fed from the low-voltage side. Before a power-factor test you:
choices: Assume the LV bushings are dead because the HV breaker is open
Isolate and test both sides, because the LV side may be the source
Skip LOTO if the nameplate says distribution
explanation: Opening the high side does not kill a unit fed from inverters, a generator, or another LV source. 29 CFR 1910.333 still wants every source disconnected, locked, and tested. Then the test voltage stays within the winding’s line-to-ground rating.
reference: 29 CFR 1910.333(b)(2); power-factor method, per Megger DELTA4000 applications guide

question: ATS 7.22.1.B.3 on an engine generator requires verification of:
choices: Phase rotation, phasing, and synchronized operation as the application requires
A 30-minute VLF test of the stator
explanation: The generator has to land on the bus in the right rotation and in phase when the application needs that. The insulation-resistance test is a separate item, run in accordance with IEEE 43.

question: ATS 7.22.1.B.6 calls for the engine-generator performance test to be run:
choices: Only if the polarization index fails
In place of the protective-shutdown tests
explanation: The performance test follows NFPA 110. This bank does not have NFPA 110, so no runtime or load step is taken from that standard. The insulation-resistance test and the shutdown tests are separate ATS lines.

question: NFPA 70B-2026 says maintenance information designates equipment as:
choices: Pass, fail, or exempt from records
explanation: Those three words say what the equipment can still be used for. They are not the same as the condition score of 1, 2, or 3 that sets how often it is maintained.
